qa_flag_actioned: W-M4-03 QA flag: ScatterVarietyDriver Resources.Load<Sprite>() returned null for sprites outside Resources/ folder, falling back to magenta procedural dot in built game.
acceptance_criterion: rimworld-comparison.md Dimension 1 'Environmental richness' row: 'More scatter variety (chunks, dead leaves); cluster scatter near trees/rock.' Binary acceptance: in a fresh built game the 3 scatter decals render as their real chunk/leaf/pebble sprites (NOT magenta dots). QA screenshot shows no magenta scatter.
fix_approach: Option (a) — move 3 PNGs into Assets/Resources/scatter/ and update Resources.Load path to match. Resources.Load resolves in Editor, batchmode, and player builds because Unity auto-bundles everything under Resources/. No SceneSetup edit required.

changes.change: Replaced SpriteChunk/SpriteLeaves/SpritePebble const strings (bare names) with ResourcePathChunk/ResourcePathLeaves/ResourcePathPebble ('scatter/stone_chunk_small', 'scatter/dead_leaves', 'scatter/pebble_scatter'). LoadSprite() now passes the subfolder-qualified resource path to Resources.Load<Sprite>(). Magenta dot kept as last-resort fallback with Debug.LogWarning. All placement and clustering logic unchanged.

qa_flags: STALE FORCEIMPORT ENTRIES (harmless): SceneSetup.cs ForceImportAllSprites still lists Assets/Sprites/stone_chunk_small.png, Assets/Sprites/dead_leaves.png, Assets/Sprites/pebble_scatter.png at the old path. These will produce '[SceneSetup] missing: ...' warnings during scene-regen because the PNGs have moved to Resources/scatter/. Warnings are HARMLESS — ForceImport is an editor setup tool; the player build picks up Resources/ automatically. No SceneSetup edit was made per lane contract. QA should expect 3 extra missing-file warnings in scene-regen output.

The original PNGs at Assets/Sprites/stone_chunk_small.png / dead_leaves.png / pebble_scatter.png remain on disk as dead copies (original .meta GUIDs intact). They are no longer referenced by ScatterVarietyDriver at runtime. QA may remove them in a future cleanup wave if desired.
Resources.Load is synchronous and occurs in Awake() before any frame is rendered — no async loading concern.
